quote.text: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.
quote.author: Marilyn Strathern's formulation of Goodhart's Law (1997)

stories.headline: The Copper President Wins Big, and the Count Turns Ugly
stories.dek: Hakainde Hichilema is romping to a second term on the strength of a debt rescue — but the tallying stopped for six hours amid violence, and the loser is alleging soldiers seized the count. The margin and the mistrust are both real.

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Buy It Once — No. 2 · Audio Cables
stories.headline: The Copper, the Banana and the Tray of Mud
stories.dek: The honest split: where a cable's price buys real engineering, and where it buys a story. One blind test settles more than a shelf of reviews.

stories.headline: The Race That Made a Gym Workout Into a World Ranking
stories.dek: Eight kilometres of running, eight fixed stations, identical in Singapore, London and New York. That sameness is the whole trick — it turns a Saturday workout into a personal best you can chase for the rest of your life. Two million people are now chasing it.

stories.headline: A Record Export Month, and the Question It Doesn't Answer
stories.dek: Non-oil exports leapt 24.2 per cent in July and the trade agency tripled its forecast for the year. Strip out the AI chips, though, and the rest of what Singapore sells the world is shrinking.

stories.headline: The Chips Are Banned. The Compute Isn't.
stories.dek: Washington spent two years walling off the hardware. It turns out Chinese labs never needed to own the chips — they can rent them by the hour, one border over, entirely within the law.

stories.headline: The First Real AR Glasses You Can Actually Order
stories.dek: Snap's Specs beat Meta, Apple and Google to a standalone true-AR consumer launch — no phone, no puck, two chips on your face. At S$3,000 they are a bet dressed as a product.

stories.headline: A Diver the Colour of an Austrian Lake — and Not for Sale Here
stories.dek: Seiko's new green Prospex 1965 re-issue is the sweet-spot heritage diver done right: in-house movement, 300 metres, forty millimetres. The catch is a border — it is a European limited edition, fourteen hundred pieces, that Singapore was not offered.

stories.headline: Six Years Quiet, and the Return Lands at Ninety-Two
stories.dek: Phoebe Bridgers' first solo album since 2020 arrived Friday to near-unanimous acclaim — a hushed grief record the critics adored. The one honest question is whether the score is about the songs or the comeback.

stories.headline: It Was Never the Hours. It's the Tail.
stories.dek: A new seven-year cohort followed children from age twelve finds the alarm belongs at the extreme — more than six hours a day — not at ordinary use. For a parent standing at the threshold with an eleven-year-old, that distinction is the whole ballgame.

stories.headline: The Data Said Cut. The Long Bond Said No.
stories.dek: Every soft print this week pointed the front end dovish — and the thirty-year still broke to its highest yield since 2007. When the measure and the market disagree, the market is telling you what the number leaves out.

stories.headline: Seventy-Five Minutes, Once a Week, Did the Same Job
stories.dek: A Hong Kong trial split the identical weekly dose three ways and found the calendar barely mattered. It is the most useful finding of the month for anyone whose week keeps eating their training.

stories.headline: Book October Now, Because October Is Already Full
The Country That Decided to Stop Importing Its Idols
stories.dek: Vietnam spent twenty years buying Korean pop. Now it is manufacturing its own boy bands on television, filling stadiums with them — and, this month, floating the studio that makes them on the stock exchange. The bookbuilding closes on 7 September.
